SNNUF SMITH & NEPHEW PLC 🌐 ✓ live实时
Smith & Nephew filed a Form 6-K attaching a TR-1 notification disclosing that Cevian Capital II GP Limited increased its aggregate voting rights in the company to 12.236% as of June 12, 2026, up from 12.074%. Cevian, an activist investment firm, holds the stake via Cevian Capital II Master Fund L.P. (11.049%) and Cevian Capital II Co-Investment - Series P L.P. (1.187%). The shares are held by Aurora Nominees as nominee. This filing signals continued activist building; the position increase suggests potential engagement on strategic direction. Watch for Cevian's next moves regarding board representation, operational changes, or a strategic review push.

2982.T AD Works Group Co., Ltd. 🌐
MI2 Corporation, Murakami Takateru, and MI5 Corporation reported a joint 10.77% stake in AD Works Group Co., Ltd. (2982.T), up from 9.74%. Murakami Takateru controls 8.17%, while MI2 Corporation has pledged 1,174,200 shares, or 90% of its position, as collateral for margin trading with SBI Securities. The filing proposes capital policy changes, specifically higher dividends and share buybacks, and indicates the group may increase its stake beyond 5% within three months or divest depending on price. The filing is the Japanese equivalent of a US 13D with an activist agenda focused on capital returns. AD Works can address the demand with its JPY2.2B (~$14M) in self-funding, but the 90% collateralization of MI2's position creates a structural overhang because margin calls could force the sale of nearly 2.6% of the float.

This filing is the Japanese equivalent of a US 13D with a public agenda and creates a new activist vector where AVI’s prior 8.21% stake had been passive.

ASH Ashland Inc.
Ancora Holdings Group has publicly demanded that Ashland Inc. (ASH) pursue a full-company sale, estimating a potential valuation of approximately $76 per share. This entry marks a shift from the cooperative approach of Standard Investments, which currently holds a ~10% stake in the specialty chemicals company. Ancora has signaled a willingness to launch a proxy contest in September if its demands are not met. Ashland recently appointed Bertrand Loy to its board effective May 15, while Seaport Global Securities upgraded the stock to Buy with a $75 target. This campaign introduces a control catalyst with an estimated 19% upside to the $63.61 share price, requiring PMs to track the September nomination window as the next escalation checkpoint.

CHE Chemed Corporation
Barington Capital Group has established a significant equity stake in Chemed Corporation (CHE) and is engaging management regarding potential board changes. Barington CEO James Mitarotonda has discussed the introduction of a new director to the board, though the firm is not currently seeking a spin-off or separation of the Roto-Rooter plumbing business. The company, which also operates the VITAS Healthcare hospice segment, has seen its shares decline over 20% in the past year and more than 30% from its 2024 peak. Barington’s history of advocating for business unit separations and the conglomerate structure of Chemed's unrelated segments make a future break-up campaign plausible, while the stock's 30% drawdown provides a receptive backdrop for activist pressure.

DSX Diana Shipping Inc. 🌐
Diana Shipping Inc. (DSX) is focusing its proxy campaign at Genco Shipping & Trading Limited on the election of Jens Ismar and Paul Cornell at Genco's June 18, 2026 annual meeting. DRVN Driven Brands Holdings Inc. ✓ live实时
ADW Capital Management, which beneficially owns 4.8% of Driven Brands Holdings Inc. (DRVN) via stock and options, issued a public letter demanding the board undertake a strategic review. The activist disclosed an $18.00 per share offer for the automotive aftermarket service franchisor, in which Roark Capital Group owns over 60%. ADW alleges Roark faces LP pressure in its 2012 Fund III and 2016 Fund IV and is prioritizing an Inspire Brands IPO over monetizing DRVN while earning management fees on $34B AUM. Driven Brands has seen double-digit year-to-date share price declines and is not current on financials while suffering from ballooning corporate SG&A despite divesting a major business. The activist is attacking the GP's LP-level incentives as a pressure vector to force the sponsor-controlled name into play as fund vintages age past years 12 to 15. Any board response or strategic review launch is the next catalyst for testing the $18.00 per share takeout floor.

FRMI Fermi Inc. ✓ live实时
Fermi Inc. (FRMI) is facing a consent solicitation from former CEO Toby Neugebauer to call a special shareholder meeting for the purpose of expanding the board by seven nominees. Neugebauer, who was terminated for cause on April 30, 2026, controls 22.7% of common stock, with an aggregate ownership of approximately 40.3% including family and existing board designees. The Neugebauer Group seeks to seat nominees to evaluate a sale, joint venture, or standalone strategy, while Fermi’s independent committee has engaged Innisfree M&A Incorporated to solicit the revocation of agent designations. This contest features an exceptionally high 40.3% starting ownership stake that will test whether the independent board can hold the line on its strategic review versus Neugebauer’s push for an immediate sale. The consent bar under Texas law and a May 13 supermajority bylaw amendment are likely the key battlefronts for this control contest.

GCO Genesco Inc. ✓ live实时
Genesco Inc. (GCO) and activist investor Bradley L. Radoff is nominating a slate of director candidates after the Genesco board rejected a settlement framework during a June 1 special meeting. FREVS First Real Estate Investment Trust of New Jersey, Inc.
The board of First Real Estate Investment Trust of New Jersey, Inc. (FREVS) approved a plan of voluntary liquidation that requires majority stockholder approval at a special meeting expected in Fall 2026. Upon approval, the company will sell its remaining portfolio of shopping centers and multifamily properties, pay off debt, and distribute net proceeds to stockholders. To provide operational runway for the asset sales, FREVS extended its $10M Valley National Bank loan and $25M ConnectOne Bank loan to August 1, 2026. A third amendment to the management agreement with Hekemian & Co. established termination fees to be paid upon property sales, and the company will switch to liquidation-basis accounting upon stockholder adoption of the plan. This liquidation play requires modeling net asset value after debt repayment and Hekemian termination fees, with the Fall 2026 stockholder vote serving as the next hard catalyst.

MMTC.NS MMTC Limited 🌐
MMTC Limited (MMTC.NS) auditors issued a qualified opinion on FY26 accounts and flagged material uncertainty regarding the company’s ability to continue as a going concern. The qualification identifies an ₹82.82 crore (~$9M) provision gap on a ₹170.58 crore (~$18M) Anglo Coal liability, following a November 2025 Delhi High Court order to release ₹1,000 crore (~$105M) to the creditor. The going-concern warning follows an administrative ministry directive for the company to prepare a manpower scale-down and business exit roadmap. While FY26 net profit before tax reached ₹463.30 crore (~$49M) due to a NINL divestment escrow release, MMTC's Singapore subsidiary MTPL is now under liquidator control. The ministry-directed exit roadmap and the July 9, 2026 hearing on the ₹82.82 crore (~$9M) liability gap signal that the entity is being wound down, placing any final liability determination directly against residual shareholder funds.

Nova Minerals Ltd, an Australian company, filed a Form 15 with the SEC to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act, effective June 16, 2026, following a redomiciliation under a statutory Scheme of Arrangement. Under the Scheme, Nova Minerals became a wholly-owned subsidiary of US Holdco (Nova Minerals Corp, a Nevada corporation). Holders of Nova Minerals ordinary shares listed on the ASX received one Chess Depositary Interest per ordinary share; OTC holders received one US Holdco common share per 12 ordinary shares; ADS holders (each representing 12 ordinary shares) received one common share per ADS; Nova Minerals warrant holders received three US Holdco warrants per Nova Minerals warrant. The Scheme constituted a succession under Rule 12g-3(a). Nasdaq filed a Form 25 to delist the ADSs and warrants, while US Holdco's common stock and warrants are expected to list on NYSE American starting June 17, 2026. This filing confirms the debt-to-equity and reverse split mechanics are now fixed, with the next observable milestone being emergence from rehabilitation to re-rate the post-reorganization equity.

512065.BO Mrugesh Trading Limited 🌐
Mrugesh Trading Limited (512065.BO) filed a disclosure on June 12, 2026, notifying that its promoter entity, JRA Infrastructure Limited, has been admitted into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) by the NCLT Ahmedabad. The insolvency follows a Section 7 application by HDFC Bank as a financial creditor claiming a default of Rs 13.80 crore (~$1.65M). The NCLT appointed Rajendra Devidas Puranik as Interim Resolution Professional, triggering a moratorium on the promoter's assets and liabilities. While Mrugesh Trading stated its own operations continue in the ordinary course, JRA Infrastructure's shares in the company are now under IRP control. This freeze on promoter-level shareholding prevents the transfer, sale, or pledging of shares without NCLT approval, which can block liquidity, trigger margin calls, or delay corporate actions requiring promoter share movement.

TSEOF Trinseo PLC
Trinseo PLC (TSEOF) filed for Chapter 11 in the Southern District of Texas with a pre-packaged restructuring support agreement to eliminate approximately $2 billion of debt and reduce annual interest expense by about $140 million. The company secured $158 million in DIP financing and a new $150 million non-recourse revolver backed by trade receivables. Under the reorganization plan, existing senior secured lenders will receive nearly all equity in the reorganized company, while general unsecured claims are expected to remain unimpaired. The pre-packaged filing signals a fast-track restructuring where existing equity holders are likely wiped out under the RSA, with the post-reorg equity value dependent on the debt load at emergence and whether the OTC-traded stub retains any recovery.

3DA.AX Amaero Ltd 🌐
Amaero Ltd (3DA.AX) received Federal Court of Australia approval for share and option schemes of arrangement to re-domicile the company from Australia to Delaware, US. The schemes become legally effective upon ASIC lodgment on June 11, 2026, at which point Amaero shares will cease trading on the ASX. Amaero US HoldCo CDIs will commence deferred-settlement trading on the ASX on June 12, with normal T+2 settlement beginning June 23. The record date for the scheme is June 15, and the implementation date is June 22, 2026. Existing option holders will receive replacement options in the US HoldCo in exchange for the cancellation of their Amaero options. This compressed timetable creates a brief settlement discontinuity between the June 11 delisting and June 12 CDI trading, requiring focus on CDI mechanics and deferred settlement for those carrying the name through the effective date.

NVA.AX Nova Minerals Limited 🌐
Nova Minerals Limited (NVA.AX) is redomiciling to the United States following the June 3, 2026, sanction of schemes of arrangement by the Supreme Court of New South Wales. New parent entity Nova Minerals Corp will list common stock and warrants on the NYSE American under the tickers NVA and NVAWW. ASX shareholders receive 1-for-1 CHESS Depositary Interests (CDIs), while OTC holders convert 12:1 into NYSE common stock and Nasdaq ADS holders convert 1:1. A trading halt is currently in effect following the June 9, 2026, record date, with trading expected to resume around June 16, 2026. Ineligible foreign and non-electing small-parcel ASX holders will have their entitlements sold on-market for pro rata distribution. The transition to a domestic U.S. issuer eliminates prior ADS/CDI complexity but introduces a 12:1 consolidation for legacy OTC holders that reduces share count and may affect liquidity for that minority.

SPRU Spruce Power Holding Corporation
Spruce Power Holding Corporation (SPRU) filed a preliminary proxy statement on June 9, 2026, to reincorporate from Delaware to Texas. The proposed Texas Charter and Bylaws would permit shareholders holding at least 10% of shares to call special meetings, a right currently unavailable under the existing Delaware charter. Additionally, Texas law enables the adoption of an ownership threshold up to 3% for derivative claims and prohibits attorney fee awards in certain derivative proceedings. The reincorporation requires shareholder approval at the company's 2026 annual meeting, scheduled for 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time on August 11, 2026, with a June 16, 2026 record date.

TRLV Trulieve Cannabis Corp.
Trulieve Cannabis Corp. (TRLV) is proposing a corporate redomestication from British Columbia to Delaware via a court-approved plan of arrangement under Section 288 of the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia). The company filed preliminary proxy materials on June 12, 2026, and has scheduled a special shareholder meeting for August 5, 2026, to vote on the proposal. The record date for the meeting was June 8, 2026. Trulieve is a vertically integrated multi-state cannabis operator headquartered in Florida and currently incorporated in British Columbia. A successful redomestication would shift the legal framework from BCBCA to the Delaware General Corporation Law, and the key mechanical hook for arbitrage-oriented managers is the BCBCA dissent right allowing shareholders to demand a fair-value payout.
